episode.title: Keep absolute-path conversion usable when canonical resolution encounters a symlink loop
episode.before: At parent commit 4625ebb4b517ce51db0aa7eb92c3fea61243610f, safe_abs_path converted its input solely with Path(res).resolve(). A circular symbolic-link chain therefore raised RuntimeError instead of returning a path. Call sites depended on this helper when constructing coder file paths, normalizing repository-discovered paths, storing the repository working-tree root, converting repository-relative paths, and finding a common root.
episode.after: At commit b2bec25c2c785989d6456cb03321a61f539bcc86, safe_abs_path still prefers Path.resolve(), but catches RuntimeError and OSError and falls back to Path.absolute(), returning the resulting path as a string. A new test constructs a two-link cycle, calls the helper, and asserts that it does not raise and returns an absolute path.
episode.diff: The implementation replaced the unconditional resolve call with a guarded canonical-resolution attempt and a lexical absolute-path fallback. The commit changed aider/utils.py by four added lines and one replaced line, and added tests/basic/test_utils.py with a 15-line circular-symlink regression test. Existing call sites were unchanged and inherit the helper's fallback behavior.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is b2bec25c2c785989d6456cb03321a61f539bcc86, its parent is 4625ebb4b517ce51db0aa7eb92c3fea61243610f, and its message states that Path.resolve raises RuntimeError on circular symlinks and that RuntimeError and OSError should fall back to Path.absolute.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller b2bec25c2c785989d6456cb03321a61f539bcc86; issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0].commits and commit_show_stat

evidence_units.claim: In the parent state, safe_abs_path unconditionally executed Path(res).resolve() and returned its string representation, with no recovery path for resolution errors.
The change wraps Path(res).resolve() in a try block and, on RuntimeError or OSError, assigns Path(res).absolute() before returning the path as a string.

The added regression test creates circular links link_a -> link_b -> link_a, invokes safe_abs_path on link_a, and asserts that the returned value is absolute; reaching the assertion also demonstrates that the call did not raise.
The coder path builder joins its configured root with a relative path and passes that result through safe_abs_path before caching and using it as an absolute filename.
Repository setup passes Git-discovered repository paths and the working_tree_dir through safe_abs_path, and repository-relative path conversion uses the same helper.
evidence_units.source: git show b2bec25c2c785989d6456cb03321a61f539bcc86:aider/repo.py, repository initialization and abs_root_path

evidence_units.claim: Common-root selection uses safe_abs_path for a single file's directory, a multi-file common path, or the current working directory.
The commit modifies only aider/utils.py and adds tests/basic/test_utils.py, totaling 19 insertions and one deletion; no call-site code is changed.

A direct reproduction in the extraction environment showed that resolving a two-link circular symlink raises RuntimeError, while applying the committed RuntimeError/OSError fallback returns an absolute path naming the unresolved link.
evidence_units.source: python3 reproduction using pathlib.Path.resolve and the committed fallback logic against a temporary link_a -> link_b -> link_a cycle

evidence_units.claim: The repository's pytest regression test could not be executed in the extraction environment because the available Python installation does not contain the pytest module; no CI or status-check result was present in the GitHub evidence bundle.
evidence_units.source: python3 -m pytest -q tests/basic/test_utils.py returned 'No module named pytest'; issue-bundle.json metadata_unavailable and limitations

candidate_atomics.name: fallback-to-lexical-absolute-path-on-resolution-failure
candidate_atomics.title: Fall back to a lexical absolute path when canonical resolution fails
candidate_atomics.description: Preserve normal canonical path resolution, but convert the original input to an absolute path without resolving symlinks when resolution raises an anticipated path-resolution exception.

semantic_action.intent: Return a usable absolute path instead of propagating an exception when canonical resolution encounters a circular symlink or another covered operating-system resolution error.
semantic_action.pre_state: A path-like input is being converted to an absolute string, and canonical resolution may raise RuntimeError or OSError.
semantic_action.post_state: Successful resolutions remain canonicalized; covered resolution failures instead produce a string-form absolute path without requiring symlink resolution.
semantic_action.validation: Construct a circular symbolic-link chain, invoke the normalization boundary on one link, verify that no exception escapes, and verify that the result is absolute.
parameters: covered resolution exceptions: RuntimeError and OSError

candidate_workflows.name: make-absolute-path-normalization-resilient-to-resolution-failures
candidate_workflows.title: Make absolute-path normalization resilient to symlink-resolution failures
candidate_workflows.description: Harden a shared path-normalization boundary by retaining canonical resolution for ordinary paths while supplying an absolute, non-resolving fallback for circular symlinks and other explicitly covered resolution failures.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure consumers of a shared absolute-path helper receive an absolute path rather than an exception when canonical path resolution cannot complete.
when_to_use: A shared helper currently relies on canonical path resolution and a reproducible circular symbolic-link input causes that boundary to raise.
Downstream consumers require an absolute path, but do not require the fallback result to dereference every symlink.
anti_goals: Do not replace canonical resolution on the successful path.
Do not claim that the fallback identifies the physical filesystem target or validates path existence.
Do not broaden the change to unrelated repository-root discovery or path-containment behavior.
Do not suppress exceptions outside the explicitly selected resolution-failure classes.
not_applicable_when: The caller requires a fully canonical, dereferenced, existing path and cannot safely accept a lexical absolute path.
The failure occurs before the shared normalization boundary is reached.
Returning a non-canonical absolute path would weaken a security or containment check.
inputs: A path input that reproduces the resolution failure
The exception classes emitted by the canonical resolver
Call sites' requirement for absolute versus canonical path semantics
workflow_graph.entry_state: Canonical resolution is the only conversion path, so a circular symlink can prevent the helper from returning any value to its callers.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The helper preserves canonical results when resolution succeeds and returns a lexical absolute-path string when resolution raises RuntimeError or OSError; the circular-symlink regression oracle completes without an exception and observes an absolute result.

steps.condition: Canonical path resolution raises one of the evidence-supported resolution exceptions and downstream semantics permit a non-canonical absolute result.
steps.validation: Exercise a two-link circular symlink and confirm both non-raising behavior and an absolute returned path.

validation_ladder: Reproduce that canonical resolution of a circular symlink raises at the normalization boundary.
Run the focused regression oracle that creates a circular symlink, calls the helper, and checks that the result is absolute.
Inspect unchanged callers to confirm they continue to use the hardened shared boundary for coder paths, repository paths, working-tree roots, and common-root conversion.
Run the broader path and repository test suites when the project's test dependencies are available.
stop_conditions: Stop if the failure cannot be reproduced at the shared normalization boundary.
Stop if affected callers require canonical or dereferenced identity rather than merely an absolute path.
Stop if the proposed fallback could be used for a security-sensitive containment decision without separate validation.
Defer completion if the focused regression test cannot be run in an environment with the project's test dependencies.
unresolved_or_deferred: The added repository test directly covers RuntimeError from a symlink loop but does not independently force the OSError branch.
The test asserts absoluteness and non-raising behavior, but not the exact fallback value or preservation of the unresolved link name.
Repository pytest execution and broader-suite validation are deferred because pytest is unavailable in the extraction environment and the evidence bundle contains no CI results.
The evidence does not establish behavior on platforms where creating symbolic links requires additional privileges.

unresolved_questions: Does every OSError emitted by Path.resolve represent a condition for which returning Path.absolute is safe, or should the fallback eventually be narrowed by errno or caller requirements?
Should future tests assert the exact lexical fallback path in addition to checking that it is absolute?
Do any security-sensitive callers treat safe_abs_path output as canonical identity or as proof that a path remains within a trusted root?
